content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository pulp-platform_riscv-dbg_pr90, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
# abstract cmd error? or a typo?  when two dscratch implemented
Hi sir, I find there may be wrong in the code below:
1. the comment is  "store a0 in dscratch1" while used the "dm::csrr" which means that read a csr(dscratch1) and store it into a0.  so the code or comment maybe wrong here!
https://github.com/pulp-platform/riscv-dbg/blob/3670267ab150f5a95e773bc18b1814e4031dc508/src/dm_mem.sv#L357
2. the senario in which can execute a abstract cmd is executing this sequence : "_entry" , "going", "whereto" and going into abstract cmd.  codes can be expanded bellow (assume dscratch1 implemented ):
_entry:
....
going:
#ifdef SND_SCRATCH
sw zero, GOING(a0)          // When debug module sees this write, the GO flag is reset.
**csrr a0, CSR_DSCRATCH1      // Restore a0 here**  **_where CSR_DSCRATCH1 contains the original value of a0_**
#else
sw zero, GOING(zero)          // When debug module sees this write, the GO flag is reset.
#endif
csrr s0, CSR_DSCRATCH0      // Restore s0 here
jal zero, whereto
// store a0 in dscratch1
dm::csrr(dm::CSR_DSCRATCH1, 5'd10)   **@AbstractCmdBaseAddr the first instruction**
here the values of CSR_DSCRATCH1 and a0 are the same (see the csrr a0, .. above)
so why should we move data between CSR_DSCRATCH1 & a0 when thay already the same?
so I think here no csr instruction is needed at all,   what do you think?
......

<analysis>
The user’s issue centers on a mismatch between comments and CSR instructions in the “two-scratch” abstract‐command generator (p_abstract_cmd_rom) within dm_mem.sv. In particular, the lines
  • “// store a0 in dscratch1” followed by a dm::csrr(DSCRATCH1, 5’d10)  
are wrong: either the comment should say “restore a0 from dscratch1,” or the instruction should be csrw.  

Walking through the code, you see:

1. The default sequence (lines ~335–343) uses csrr(DSCRATCH1, x10) to *restore* a0 after setting up the DM base address. This is correct, but the surrounding comments deserve inspection to ensure they reflect *restore*, not *store*.

2. In the AccessRegister → transfer & write case (lines ~354–362):
   - The comment at line 356 says “store a0 in dscratch1” 
   - The code on line 357 is a csrr (read) 
   This is clearly the restore operation (not store), so the comment must be changed to “restore a0 from dscratch1.”

3. In the AccessRegister → transfer & !write case (lines ~395–403):
   - The comment at line 396 is again “store a0 in dscratch1”
   - The code on line 398 uses csrr
   Again, this comment needs to be updated to “restore a0 from dscratch1.”

4. It’s also worth inspecting the definition of LoadBaseAddr and HasSndScratch (around lines 63–67) to ensure the correct register number (x10) is used for the csrr/​csrw operations in the two-scratch case.

Hence at least three edit/inspection points are:
  • The default abstract_cmd[4] restore (lines 335–343) – verify comment/semantics  
  • The write‐transfer branch (lines 354–362) – fix comment to “restore”  
  • The read‐transfer branch (lines 395–403) – fix comment to “restore”  
  • Optionally, the LoadBaseAddr definition (lines 63–67) if you need to adjust which register is used  
</analysis>
